key_insight: Decision models can take on structured clinical tasks, but they need task-specific prompting and may work best as a hybrid with LLMs.
clinical_relevance: In clinical NLP workflows, using a cheaper decision model for high-confidence cases and an LLM for the rest could reduce cost while preserving performance.
method: Compared Jev against five flagship LLMs on mortality risk, Choosing-Wisely categorization, and colon cancer staging.
Tested standard LLM-style prompting versus developer-recommended input changes, including medical context and task decomposition.
Evaluated a hybrid strategy that routed fully confident staging predictions to Jev and the remaining cases to LLMs.
evidence_signal: With standard prompting, Jev underperformed LLMs, but improved staging accuracy from 45.4% to 85.8% with both input changes, and the hybrid approach cut flagship LLM costs by 33-44% while remaining non-inferior.
watch_item: Performance depended strongly on prompt design, and staging errors were more common when Jev was not fully confident, so workflow integration needs careful validation.
paper_title: Decision models can offload structured clinical tasks from large language models
